newsitem.title: USA: Goodyear contract ratified, ending strike.
newsitem.headline: Goodyear contract ratified, ending strike.

text.p: Goodyear Tire & Rubber Co Inc and the United Steelworkers of America union said late Thursday night that a six-year labor agreement has been ratified, ending a strike by nearly 13,000 U.S. rubber workers that began April 20.

Under the pact, workers will get a 29-cent wage increase on January 1, 1998 as a result of a restored cost of living allowance. In addition, employees will receive a general wage increase of 35 cents an hour on January 1, 1999.

"Our Master Contract Locals at Goodyear are to be commended for their solidarity and spirit in negotiating a meaningful agreement that will carry them into the 21st Century," union President George Becker said in a statement. "This agreement represents a significant achievement of goals for both our USWA Goodyear Council and the company.
"We have demonstrated our mettle and this agreement will benefit Steelworker families at Goodyear for many years to come," Becker added.
In a separate statement, Goodyear Chairman and Chief Executive Sam Gibara said he was pleased with the ratification vote.
"The new agreement supports our ability to implement the business strategy we need to carry Goodyear into the 21st century," Gibara said.
The strike was the first to hit Goodyear since a 140-day work stoppage that paralyzed the tire industry in 1976.
